content:
In the past few days, there have been two reports pointing out that Apple can boost its services revenue through different avenues to earn more money.

In my view, Apple absolutely should do the first one, but not the second — and it seems Phil Schiller may well agree with that take…

First let me summarise these two reports.

Home security and monitoring services

On Friday, Bloomberg reported that Apple may be planning to launch an entirely new home security and monitoring service, to go with some new home hardware we're expecting.

Squeezing more revenue from the App Store

The same source's second report on Sunday said Apple is exploring ways to squeeze more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple should not do the latter

On the contrary, I think the second approach would be a very big mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly on iPhone app sales has come under fire from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell an iPhone app, you have to do it through the official App Store, so you have no choice but to take whatever terms Apple offers on a take-it-or-leave-it basis.

I understand the common view that nobody forces anyone to buy an iPhone or develop an app for it, but that isn't how even the most laissez-faire form of capitalism works in practice: even in the US, there have been antitrust laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, restrictions are placed on what you can do to ensure you don't abuse your position.

Trying to squeeze more money out of the App Store is entirely the opposite of 'skating to where the puck is going', a view reportedly shared by Phil Schiller, which Bloomberg notes is one of the reasons he's stepping back now.

Innovative services are the right direction

By contrast, launching entirely new and innovative services that people want to buy is what Apple should be doing. I can completely see the value of the company offering a home security monitoring service.

I argued back in 2024 that making its own smart home cameras would be one of the … smartest things the company could do. The same goes for the rumoured Apple smart doorbell. Offering an optional service bundle for security products makes complete sense, for two reasons.

First, all the privacy arguments I previously made. HomeKit Secure Video has already done a great deal to ensure the privacy of security camera footage. If I were going to pick a company to do AI analysis of security camera footage, I would trust Apple.

Second, Apple is of course best placed to fully integrate the security hardware and service within the HomeKit environment. I believe there are many other areas where Apple could offer a similar benefit.

For me, the key is that Apple needs to take the same approach to services as it does to hardware. Make great products that people are happy, even eager, to pay for. Not try to extract money in ways that antagonise customers, developers, and regulators alike.

What are your thoughts on this? Please share your views in the comments.
